General Knowledge 2017-I.question: Which one of the following statements is correct? For the purpose of Census 2011
options: a person aged seven and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as a literate
a person aged eight and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as a literate
a person aged nine and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as a literate
a person aged ten and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as a literate
General Knowledge 2017-I.answer: a person aged seven and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as a literate
General Knowledge 2017-I.explanation: (a)  In 2011 Census, a person aged seven years and above who can both read and write in any language, is treated as ‘literate’. In the Censuses prior to 1991, children below five years of age were treated as illiterates, but later, keeping in mind that the ability to read and write with understanding is not generally achieved until one has time to develop these skills, the defining age for the literate category was raised to seven in the Censuses of 2001 and 2011. 119. General Knowledge 2017-I.question: The Most Favoured Nation (MFN) Clause under WTO regime is based on the principle of
options: differential treatment between locals and foreigners
General Knowledge 2017-I.explanation: (a)  Most-favoured-nation (MFN) Clause under the WTO regime ensured that countries should not discriminate between their trading nations and also that national and international business entities get equal treatment. The clause forms the first article of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). Reducing tariffs and non-tariff barriers is also highlighted by the clause.
